newsitem.title: USA: SEC probes US Diagnostic, execs on leave.
newsitem.headline: SEC probes US Diagnostic, execs on leave.

text.p: US Diagnostic Inc said on Monday that the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Nasdaq Stock Market Inc have initiated inquiries focusing on the company's former relationship with Coyote Consulting and Financial Services LLC and Keith Greenberg, as well as the adequacy of the company's disclosure concerning that relationship.

The company said that Jeffrey Goffman, chairman and chief executive officer, and Michael Karsch, the company's general counsel, have been placed on administrative leave by the company's board of directors.

The company has set up a special committee consisting of the company's three outside directors to investigate and act on the company's behalf in all matters relating to Coyote and Greenberg, including authority to take appropriate disciplinary action with respect to officers and employees of the company.

Laurans Mendelson, one of the outside directors, has been named chairman of its board of directors and Joseph Paul, the company's president and chief operating officer, has been given the additional post of interim chief executive officer.
Mendelson is the chairman, president and chief executive officer of HEICO Corp, which sold its MediTek Health Corp subsidiary to US Diagnostic in July 1996.

According to US Diagnostic, the SEC and Nasdaq inquiries are being conducted to determine whether the company's and management's disclosures with respect to Greenberg and Coyote have been in compliance with the federal securities laws and NASDAQ's listing standards.
The company said it is cooperating fully with both inquiries.
US Diagnostics said it intends to proceed with its previously announced transactions and continue to aggressively pursue the acquisition candidates currently under review.

The company said it expects to complete the acquisition of Medical Diagnostic upon obtaining Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust approval and that the above events are not expected to impact the company's operations or its financial condition.
In January, Advanced NMR Systems Inc and US Diagnostic said they were in a definitive deal to sell Advanced NMR's Medical Diagnostic Inc unit to US Diagnostic for $22 million.
